summary: A 1970 proposal to change the host-IMP specification to eliminate marking, by W. R. Crowther. It is a design suggestion for the interface between a host and its IMP.

eli5.summary: A suggestion to simplify how a computer and its network box talk by dropping something unneeded.

subtitle: BBN proposes sending the host/IMP message leader and text as two consecutive messages to end marking problems.

tldr.problem: The host/IMP specification packed the leader and text of a message together, which caused what the note calls marking problems on hosts with different word lengths.
tldr.mechanism: Separate the leader from the text and send them as consecutive messages, so the text always starts on a word boundary, in both IMP-to-Host and Host-to-IMP directions.
tldr.outcome: BBN saw no disadvantages and tentatively planned to implement it, with modified Host spec text and one week of notice.

today: RFC 67 is a proposal from January 1970, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text says only that BBN tentatively planned to implement the change, not whether it did.

sections.title: The Marking Problem
sections.content:
W. Crowther of BBN reports that Dave Walden, before leaving for Norway, observed a simple change to the Host/IMP specifications that would eliminate all of the so-called marking problems. The text does not define marking further.

The aim is that message text should start on a word boundary no matter what the word lengths of the machines involved are.
sections.eli5: Different computers chop data into different sized pieces, so things did not line up neatly. The idea is to make sure every message starts exactly at the start of a piece.

sections.title: Sending the Leader Separately
sections.content:
The change is to separate the leader from the text of regular messages and send them as consecutive messages instead of one packed message. Because the text then starts on a word boundary, the sizes of the hosts' words stop mattering.

The process would take place on both IMP-to-Host and Host-to-IMP messages.
sections.eli5: Instead of writing the address and the letter on one sheet, you put them on two sheets and send them one after the other.

sections.title: Reaction and Rollout
sections.content:
BBN could see no disadvantages, and a sampling of Host reactions ranged from neutral to wildly enthusiastic. It therefore tentatively planned to implement the change.

The note recognizes that the change requires Host program changes, so the new release must be scheduled to coincide with them. BBN proposed providing modified Host spec text along with a one week notice of the new release, and asked anyone who saw a flaw to contact BBN quickly, since a new version of the IMP program was already in the works.
sections.eli5: The people who made the network boxes asked, does anybody hate this idea? Nobody did, so they planned to do it and promised to warn everyone a week ahead.
